title: Applied ML Evals: Unified Onboarding, Prompt Sets, Quantization Profiles, and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Maya Singh
summary: A single reference playbook that defines the end-to-end Applied ML evals workflow at Redwood: eval harness onboarding, prompt set and benchmark standards, model onboarding checklist, quantization profile process, quality guardrails, and regression triage procedures.
body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates the core operational procedures and standards used by Applied ML, Model Onboarding, and the Eval Harness teams to evaluate, onboard, and maintain models in Redwood’s serving fleet. It covers:

- Eval harness onboarding and continuous evaluation best practices
- Prompt set and benchmark creation standards
- Model onboarding checklist for production serving
- Quantization profile creation and verification procedures
- Quality guardrails and monitoring signals
- Regression triage and incident response workflow

Audience

This document is intended for ML engineers, SREs, model owners, and platform engineers responsible for model onboarding, evaluation, and production quality.

Ownership and SLAs

- Owner: Applied ML & Evals (engineering)
- Primary contact: maya.singh@redwood.ai
- Expected review cadence: Quarterly
- Onboarding SLO: new model onboarding <= 10 business days from CLA sign-off to first internal evaluation run

1) Eval Harness Onboarding and Continuous Evaluation

Introduction
The eval harness is the canonical system for running deterministic evaluation suites against candidate model checkpoints and quantized variants. Onboarding a model to the harness triggers baseline measurements used for rollout decisions.

Required metadata for harness runs:

- model_id (string)
- model_version (string)
- commit_hash (git sha)
- run_tags: ["onboarding", "regression-check", "quantized"]
- dataset_ids (list)

Onboarding steps (numbered):

1. Create an eval ticket and link RFC + model artifacts.
2. Register model metadata in model-registry with owner and risk classification.
3. Add basic prompt sets (see Section 2) and define primary metrics (ROUGE, BLEU, perplexity, embedding-similarity).
4. Run full harness: functional tests, safety checks (toxicity, hallucination detectors), latency/throughput microbenchmarks.
5. Compare against baseline model and record delta table in the harness results.
6. If gating thresholds are met, mark candidate as ready for quantization/testing on Dedicated pools.

Important CLI examples

- Run an onboarding suite (example):

  conda activate eval-harness
  eval-run --model=redwood/gpt-small:2026-11-28 --suite=onboarding-full --out=/tmp/run-2026-11-28.json

- Sample JSON config for a harness run:

  {
    "model_id": "redwood/gpt-small",
    "model_version": "2026-11-28",
    "suites": ["onboarding-full", "safety-smoke"],
    "max_tokens": 512
  }

2) Prompt Sets and Benchmarks

Principles

- Representativeness: prompt sets must reflect production query distributions, business-critical tasks, and edge cases.
- Size and reproducibility: each benchmark should have a clear seed and deterministic sampling method.
- Ownership: each prompt set must have an owner and a documented update cadence.

Prompt set structure (recommended fields):

- id: short-handle
- owner: team/email
- description: short purpose statement
- provenance: source (prod-sampled, synthetic, partner-provided)
- seed & sampling method
- labels: list of tags (e.g., "summarization", "code", "customer-data")

Benchmarking guidance

- Small smoke sets (50-200 prompts) for CI checks.
- Core benchmarks (1k-10k prompts) for gating.
- Long-tail sets: curated by product to capture critical edge cases.

Example table: (CSV-like format)

| prompt_set_id | size | owner | primary_metric | update_frequency |
| onboarding-smoke | 100 | applied-ml | accuracy+latency | weekly |
| doc-summarization-core | 5000 | search-team | Rouge-L | quarterly |

3) Model Onboarding Checklist (to serving-ready)

Pre-reqs (before request for production capacity):

- Model artifacts stored in S3 and registered in model-registry.
- Security review completed (data leakage, PII handling).
- Training and eval logs uploaded to the experiment tracker.
- Cost estimate and resource profile documented (GPU type, vCPU, memory, expected qps).

Checklist (tick-box style in Confluence):

- [ ] Harness onboarding run completed and passed gating thresholds
- [ ] Safety & privacy scan passed
- [ ] Quantized variants evaluated (if applicable)
- [ ] Performance tests for tail latencies and cold-starts executed
- [ ] Rolling deploy plan documented (canary percentages, rollback criteria)
- [ ] Ownership assigned and runbook created

Rollout guidance

- Canary: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with at least 24h between steps and health checks at each step.
- Automatic rollback triggers: >3% increase in error rate, >10% regression in primary quality metric, or violation of latency SLOs.

4) Quantization Profiles and Verification

When quantizing a model, the quantization owner should produce a profile that documents:

- strategy: INT8/FP16/LLM.int4, per-channel/per-tensor
- calibration data used (prompt_set_id)
- accuracy delta tolerances (absolute and relative)
- performance gains (tokens/sec, GPU memory)

Quantization workflow (high level):

1. Create calibration prompt set (sample 5-10k representative prompts).
2. Run quantization toolchain to produce candidate artifacts.
3. Run copy of eval harness: functional, safety, and long-tail benchmarks against quantized artifact.
4. If metrics within tolerances, run Dedicated-pool perf validation (throughput/latency).
5. Stamp profile into model-registry and document in the quantization-profiles directory.

Verification criteria (example):

- Absolute ROUGE-L drop <= 0.5 points on core benchmark OR relative drop <= 2%
- Latency improvement >= 15% or memory reduction >= 30% required to proceed unless business justifies otherwise

5) Quality Guardrails and Monitoring Signals

Guardrails to check continuously (SLO-driven):

- Latency SLO: p99 < 800ms for hosted small models; p99 < 1200ms for larger models (see performance-standards).
- Error rate: HTTP 5xx < 0.1% baseline; any increase > 0.5% triggers incident process.
- Quality regression alert: >5% relative regression in primary quality metric on sampled production prompts over a 24h window.
- Safety alert: increase in flagged toxicity tokens by >250% relative to baseline.

Monitoring setup (recommended panels):

- Token-level cost & latency by route/model
- Quality delta trend (7d, 24h) for primary metrics
- Safety flags (rate and top-k examples)
- Regression triage dashboard linking to recent harness runs and prompt-set diffs

6) Regression Triage Playbook

Purpose

Define a fast, reproducible process for diagnosing and mitigating quality regressions detected by the harness or production monitoring.

Triage steps (sequence):

1. Triage lead (oncall from Applied ML) acknowledges alert and creates a triage incident in the tracker.
2. Gather signal: harness run diffs, production-sampled examples, model versions, recent config/infra changes.
3. Classify regression: dataset shift, model change, quantization side-effect, infra degradation, or prompt routing regression.
4. Quick mitigations: rollback to previous model, increase fallback routing, or apply conservative decoding/temp/penalty changes.

Root-cause analysis (RCA) checklist:

- Reproduce issue locally with the smallest failing prompt set.
- Check quantized vs. fp32 differences; run comparative scoring.
- Validate that model weights/artifacts match the expected commit-hash.
- Review recent prompt-set changes or sampling weight updates.

Post-incident actions

- Document RCA and corrective action in the incident tracker within 48 hours.
- Update prompt sets or harness tests if a gap is found.
- If model was faulty, add a new blocking test to the harness.

Appendices

A. Example harness diff summary (table-like):

| metric | baseline | candidate | delta | action |
| Rouge-L | 34.2 | 33.8 | -0.4 | accept (within tolerance) |
| Safety: toxicity rate | 0.12% | 0.25% | +0.13% | block (investigate) |
